 More than 135,000 property tax statements have been mailed to Galveston County property owners, with several payment options available ahead of the 2026 tax deadlines.
 Galveston County Tax Assessor-Collector Cheryl E. Johnson announced that property owners have until Feb. 1, 2027, to pay their taxes in full without penalties or interest.
 Residents also can choose a split-payment option, paying half their taxes by Nov. 30 and the remaining balance by June 30, 2027.
 Senior citizens, people with disabilities, disabled veterans and property owners affected by governor-declared disasters may qualify to pay their taxes in four equal installments. Those payments are due Feb. 1, March 31, June 1 and Aug. 2.
 Property owners whose mortgage companies handle property taxes through escrow accounts will not receive mailed statements.
 Payments can be made online through the county tax office website, by mail, by telephone or in person at county tax offices.
 Online payments made by electronic check carry a 50-cent bank fee, while credit and debit card transactions are subject to a 2.2% fee.
 Residents mailing payments should ensure they are postmarked by the applicable deadline. Yellow payment drop boxes also are available outside full-time county tax offices.
 Payments deposited in those boxes before 8 a.m. Dec. 1 will be credited as received Nov. 30.
 County tax offices are located in Galveston, Texas City, Santa Fe, League City and Friendswood, with additional satellite services available in Crystal Beach.
 For more information about payment options, deadlines or office locations, residents can call 877-766-2284 or visit the Galveston County Tax Office website.
